area: F5 CP-SAT (cycle A, claims first): Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/*, Tests/ZTronLPCPSATTests/**, SATLIB uf50/uuf50, pure-integer MIPLIB 3

findings.title: In-domain data of magnitude >= 2^49 is silently rounded by a 4-ulp snap tolerance: infeasible points and wrong optima labelled .optimal
findings.claim: README §2.5 CPSAT row: throws .unsupported only for ... 'bounds or scaled coefficients of magnitude 2^53 or more, or row activities beyond +-2^61'; README §4 Limits/CP-SAT: data accepted 'with bounds and scaled coefficients below 2^53 and row activities within +-2^61'; CPModel.swift header: 'CP-SAT works on pure integer programs in exact Int64 arithmetic', root domains 'rounded inward', fractional row bounds 'round inward'; README §4 Results: optimal means feasible to 1e-7; README risk 10: exact for integral costs below 1e4.
findings.observed: (a) x fixed by xl=xu=2^52+1, y in [0,10], row x + y <= 2^52+1, maximize y (only feasible y is 0): .optimal obj=8, x=[4503599627370493 (=2^52-3), 8]; CompiledLP.maxViolation = bounds 4, rows 4 (det, par, detnolp). (b) (1e15+0.5)x + y >= 1e15+1, x binary, y in [0,3], min y (true optimum 1): .optimal obj=0, x=[1,0], maxViolation rows 0.5. (c) max x with x in [0, 2^52+1]: .optimal x=2^52+5 (bound +4); 2^51+1 -> 2^51+3; 2^50+1 -> 2^50+2; mirrored for lower bounds. (d) rows x <= 2^50+1 / 2^52+1 return 2^50+2 / 2^52+5; a=2^40+1, x<=1e6, a*x <= 989560464999299968 returns x=900000 (exact max 899999). (e) the effective rejection limit is not 2^53: xu=2^53-1 and 2^53-4 throw .unsupported 'too large', xu=2^53-5 returns x=2^53-1 (bound and row +4).
findings.whyWrong: All data is exactly representable, below 2^53, with activities far inside +-2^61, i.e. inside the documented domain, so it must be solved exactly or rejected. CPModel.snapTolerance = max(1e-9, 4*ulp(v)) counts any value within 4 ulp of an integer as that integer and is added outward to column bounds and row sides; at |v| >= 2^49 that is 0.5 to 4 units, so the integer model searched is a widened one. The returned points violate the model as given (visible in Double, reported by the package's own maxViolation), and in (a) and (b) the objective is wrong by 8 and by 1 at objective values far below 1e4. The end-of-solve self-check CPSAT.violation uses a 1e-6 relative tolerance and cannot see violations of a few units at 1e15. Trigger is narrow (data >= ~5.6e14), but the answer is a wrong .optimal.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/CPModel.swift:117-119 (snapTolerance), applied at :131 (integralScale), :173-174 (column bounds), :335 and :347 (row sides); Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/LPRelaxation.swift:95,99; self-check Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/CPSAT.swift:340-354

findings.title: A coefficient that no power of 10 up to 1e6 makes integral (1e-10) is zeroed instead of rejected, and the solve ends in SolverError.internalInconsistency
findings.claim: README §2.5 CPSAT and CPSAT.solve doc: throws .unsupported for 'data that no power of 10 up to 1e6 makes integral'. CPSAT.run: a point that fails the final check is 'A bug, never a property of the model'.
findings.observed: max x + y s.t. 1e-10 x + y <= 1, x in [0,1e9], y in [0,1]: THROW 'internal inconsistency: CP-SAT returned a point that violates row c1' in det, par and detnolp. 1e-10 x <= 0.05, x in [0,1e9]: internalInconsistency (par), det climbs to the time limit. Control cases behave: 1e-7 and (4e-10, 1e-6) are rejected with .unsupported.
findings.whyWrong: integralScale accepts |v*scale - round(v*scale)| <= max(1e-9, 4 ulp), so 1e-10 is the integer 0 at scale 1 and the term is dropped; CP-SAT then solves a different model and its self-check reports a solver bug. The documented outcome for such data is .unsupported; an internalInconsistency error tells the user the solver is broken.

findings.documented: The 1e-9 snap is stated only in the CPModel.swift header comment ('integral within 1e-9'); README states rejection; the internalInconsistency outcome is not documented.

findings.title: Tests named for large-data handling and inward rounding never reach the magnitudes where A5-01 fails
findings.claim: LPPropagatorTests.dataNearTheLimitsOfInt64IsHandled ('push the integer combination towards the limits of Int64 ... the answer does not change'); AcceptanceTests.scalingToleratesFloatingPointNoiseOnly ('A large value that is not an integer is not mistaken for one'); AcceptanceTests.columnBoundsRoundInward; AcceptanceTests.largeButRepresentableDataIsAccepted.
findings.observed: The largest data these tests use: activities of 1e15 (below 2^50), a fractional value 1.2e11, column bounds below 4. In the documented domain the named properties fail: 1e15+0.5 is taken as an integer (A5-01 b), bounds >= 2^50 round outward (A5-01 c). The suites pass in the baseline (debug, release, TSAN).
findings.whyWrong: Each test can only pass for data below 2^49, so none can catch the defect it is named for; the documented limits (2^53, 2^61) are only tested on the rejection side.

findings.title: winningWorker of a parallel feasibility solve can name a worker whose solution was not the one returned
findings.claim: CPSATAnalysis.winningWorker doc (CPSAT.swift:372-375): 'the one that completed the proof (or, for a feasibility problem, found the solution)'.
findings.observed: CPSAT(workers: 8) on the first 100 uf50-218 files: in 23 runs winningWorker is cpsat[0] or cpsat[1] while the only .newIncumbent event, whose model the store kept and returned, came from another worker (uf50-0104: winner 0, source cpsat[6]; uf50-0103: winner 0, source cpsat[2]).
findings.whyWrong: run() picks the lowest-index report with outcome .satisfied (CPSAT.swift:259, :331) while the IncumbentStore keeps the first model offered and rejects later ones of equal objective (Portfolio.swift:68-69), so the field does not identify the worker that found the reported solution.

findings.title: bound differs from objectiveValue on .optimal results, contrary to two doc comments
findings.claim: CPSATAnalysis doc (CPSAT.swift:361-362): 'bound is the propagated bound of the objective row, and equals objectiveValue once optimality is proven'; SolutionAnalysis.bound (Analysis.swift:22): 'Proven bound; equals objectiveValue when optimal'.
findings.observed: .optimal obj=3.500001 bound=3.500007 (max 1e-6 x + 3.5, x in [0,7]); .optimal obj=562946402850150 bound=562949953421313 (max x, x <= 2^49+1, parallel); .optimal obj=-2.3795703474867405e+17 bound=-2.3796833534450074e+17 (large-coefficient model, det).
findings.whyWrong: When the gap closes without exhaustion, run() deliberately reports the proven bound (CPSAT.swift:298-303), so .optimal does not imply bound == objectiveValue; a caller following the doc comments can read the wrong number.

findings.documented: README risk 10 documents that .optimal means within the gap, but not that bound and objectiveValue then differ; the two doc comments state the opposite.

overflow: A NaN row upper bound is silently treated as no bound (max x, x<=5, row x <= NaN -> optimal 5) instead of an error (F5_ONLY=D11 domain).

deterministic: true with the default lpPropagator: true also climbs one step per incumbent when the model has no linear row for the relaxation (bounds only or clause rows only); the CPSAT doc names only lpPropagator: false (D5 det: feasible(timeLimit) at 2.6e6 of 5.6e14 after 20 s, parallel solves it at once).

README risk 10 advice 'keep objective values below 10^4' is not enough with non-integral costs or a large objective constant: max 1e-6x + 3.5 returns x=1 instead of 7 labelled optimal (within the documented gap; the CPSAT doc comment states the step rule correctly).

Cross-area, for the branch-and-bound/simplex finder: BranchAndBound(deterministic: true) on the A5-01 model (x fixed at 2^52+1, x + y <= 2^52+1, max y) returns optimal obj=10 with x=4503599577830908, a fixed bound violated by 4.95e7 (F5 xcheck).

SATTests run only the first 100 of 1000 files of each SATLIB family; a missing corpus disables them through .enabled(if:) rather than recording the known issue the HANDBOOK describes (my probe ran all 2000 files: all pass).
A deterministic run that stops at its time limit is not reproducible (p0201 detnolp 1 s: 9595, 9535, 9595), although the CPSAT doc says 'identical results'; this is inherent to wall-clock limits.
summary: The CDCL core holds up on everything checked: all 2,000 SATLIB uf50/uuf50 instances (uuf cross-checked by an independent DPLL), 1,200 random 3-SAT formulas, about 3,000 small and mid-size integer programs against exhaustive enumeration across 10 configurations (LP propagator on and off, deterministic, 2 and 8 workers, no sharing, every restart policy, tight memory budgets, hints), wide domains against an exact oracle, the 7 pure-integer MIPLIB 3 optima, determinism, time limits and cancellation. The serious defect is in loading the model: a 4-ulp snap tolerance silently rounds in-domain data at magnitudes of 2^49 or more (about 5.6e14). The result is wrong answers labelled .optimal, for example objective 8 where only 0 is feasible, with bounds and rows violated by 4 (A5-01). The bound limit is also really 2^53-5, not the documented 2^53. A coefficient of 1e-10 is zeroed instead of rejected and ends in internalInconsistency (A5-02). The tests named for large data stop below 2^50 and cannot catch A5-01 (A5-03). There are two low-severity mismatches between the doc comments and the analysis fields (A5-04 winningWorker, A5-05 bound). The trigger for A5-01 is narrow, but the README places it inside the accepted domain.
